questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: find a missing angle in a triangle
questions.stem: A triangle has angles measuring 40 degrees and 70 degrees. What is the measure of the third angle, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The three angles of a triangle sum to 180 degrees, so the third angle is 180 minus 40 minus 70, which equals 70 degrees. Forgetting the 180-degree sum, or subtracting only one angle, are the common errors.
questions.hint: Angles in a triangle sum to 180 degrees.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Two adjacent angles form a straight angle. One angle measures 35 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees, so the missing angle is 180 minus 35, or 145 degrees. A common error is using 90 degrees instead of 180.
questions.hint: Supplementary angles sum to 180 degrees.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Two lines intersect, and one of the angles formed measures 52 degrees. What is the measure of the angle vertical to it?

options.misconception: confuses vertical angle with supplementary angle
confuses vertical angle with complementary angle
treats the vertical angle as a straight angle

questions.explanation: Vertical angles are congruent, so the vertical angle also measures 52 degrees. The other values are supplementary or complementary measures, not the vertical angle.
questions.hint: Vertical angles have equal measure.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Which statement about the interior angles of any triangle is true?

options.misconception: confuses triangle with quadrilateral angle sum
confuses triangle sum with right angle
believes angle sum varies with side lengths

questions.explanation: Every triangle's interior angles sum to 180 degrees, regardless of side lengths. Quadrilaterals sum to 360 degrees, not triangles.
questions.hint: All triangles have the same interior angle sum.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A triangle has interior angles of 40 degrees and 30 degrees at two vertices. What is the measure of the exterior angle at the third vertex, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: An exterior angle equals the sum of the two remote interior angles, so 40 plus 30 equals 70 degrees. A common error is subtracting instead of adding.
questions.hint: Exterior angle equals the sum of the remote interior angles.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: find base angles of an isosceles triangle
questions.stem: An isosceles triangle has a vertex angle of 40 degrees. What is the measure of each base angle, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The remaining 140 degrees are split equally between the two base angles, so each is 70 degrees. A common error is dividing 180 by 2 without subtracting the vertex angle.
questions.hint: Subtract the vertex angle from 180, then divide by 2.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A circle has radius 7 units. What is its circumference, in units? Use 22/7 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Circumference is 2 times pi times radius, so 2 times 22/7 times 7 equals 44 units. Using diameter instead of radius is a common error.
questions.hint: Circumference equals 2 pi r.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A circle has radius 7 units. What is its area, in square units? Use 22/7 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Area is pi times radius squared, so 22/7 times 49 equals 154 square units. A common error is using 2 pi r, the circumference formula.
questions.hint: Area equals pi r squared.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: relate central angle to arc measure
questions.stem: In a circle, a central angle measures 80 degrees. What is the measure of its intercepted arc?

options.misconception: confuses central angle with inscribed angle
confuses intercepted arc with full circle

questions.explanation: A central angle and its intercepted arc have the same measure, so the arc measures 80 degrees. Inscribed angles are half the arc measure.
questions.hint: Central angle measure equals arc measure.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: compute an inscribed angle from its arc
questions.stem: An inscribed angle intercepts an arc of 100 degrees. What is the measure of the inscribed angle, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: An inscribed angle is half the measure of its intercepted arc, so 100 divided by 2 equals 50 degrees. A common error is using the full arc measure.
questions.hint: Inscribed angle is half the intercepted arc.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: compute sector area from radius and central angle
questions.stem: A circle has radius 6 units. A sector has central angle 60 degrees. What is the area of the sector, in square units? Use 3.14 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Sector area is pi r squared times the central angle over 360, so 3.14 times 36 times 60/360 equals 18.84 square units. A common error is omitting the angle fraction.
questions.hint: Sector area = pi r^2 times (angle/360).

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A rectangle has length 12 units and width 5 units. What is its area, in square units? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Rectangle area is length times width, so 12 times 5 equals 60 square units. A common error is adding the dimensions instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Area equals length times width.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A triangle has base 10 units and height 8 units. What is its area, in square units? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Triangle area is one-half times base times height, so 0.5 times 10 times 8 equals 40 square units. A common error is forgetting the one-half factor.
questions.hint: Area equals one-half base times height.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A trapezoid has bases 8 and 12 units and height 5 units. What is its area?

options.misconception: uses only one base times height

questions.explanation: Trapezoid area is the average of the bases times height, so (8 plus 12)/2 times 5 equals 50 square units.
questions.hint: Area equals (base1 + base2)/2 times height.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A circle has diameter 10 units. What is its area, in square units? Use 3.14 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The radius is 5 units, so the area is 3.14 times 5 squared, or 78.5 square units. A common error is using the diameter directly as the radius.
questions.hint: Halve the diameter to get the radius first.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A rectangular prism has length 4 units, width 3 units, and height 5 units. What is its volume, in cubic units? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Prism volume is length times width times height, so 4 times 3 times 5 equals 60 cubic units. A common error is adding the dimensions.
questions.hint: Volume equals length times width times height.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A cylinder has radius 3 units and height 10 units. What is its volume, in cubic units? Use 3.14 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Cylinder volume is pi r squared h, so 3.14 times 9 times 10 equals 282.6 cubic units. A common error is using diameter instead of radius.
questions.hint: Volume equals pi r^2 h.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A cone has radius 3 units and height 12 units. Which expression gives its volume? Use 3.14 for pi.

options.misconception: uses cylinder volume without dividing by 3
uses radius instead of radius squared
omits radius squared and division by 3

questions.explanation: Cone volume is one-third times pi r squared h, so the correct expression divides the cylinder volume by 3. The other expressions omit a required factor.
questions.hint: Cone volume is one-third of the matching cylinder volume.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A sphere has radius 3 units. What is its volume, in cubic units? Use 3.14 for pi and round to the nearest whole number. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Sphere volume is four-thirds times pi r cubed, so 4/3 times 3.14 times 27 is about 113.04, which rounds to 113. A common error is using r squared instead of r cubed.
questions.hint: Volume equals 4/3 pi r^3.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A square pyramid has base side 6 units and height 9 units. What is its volume, in cubic units? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Pyramid volume is one-third times base area times height, so 1/3 times 36 times 9 equals 108 cubic units. A common error is omitting the one-third factor.
questions.hint: Volume equals one-third base area times height.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Point P(2, -3) is translated 4 units right and 2 units up. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: Add 4 to the x-coordinate and 2 to the y-coordinate, giving (6, -1). Sign errors in either coordinate are common.
questions.hint: Add the shift to each coordinate.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: reflect a point across the y-axis
questions.stem: A point has coordinates (5, -2). After reflection across the y-axis, what is the x-coordinate of the image? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Reflection across the y-axis negates the x-coordinate, so the image has x-coordinate -5. A common error is negating the y-coordinate instead.
questions.hint: Reflecting across the y-axis changes the sign of x.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A point (3, 4) is rotated 90 degrees counterclockwise about the origin. What are the coordinates of the image?
questions.explanation: A 90-degree counterclockwise rotation maps (x, y) to (-y, x), so (3, 4) maps to (-4, 3). Direction and sign errors are common.
questions.hint: Use the rule (x, y) becomes (-y, x).

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: A segment has length 6 units. After a dilation with scale factor 2.5, what is the length of the image, in units? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Dilation multiplies length by the scale factor, so 6 times 2.5 equals 15 units. A common error is adding the scale factor instead of multiplying.
questions.hint: Multiply the original length by the scale factor.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Which transformation is not a congruence transformation?
questions.explanation: Dilation changes size, so it is not a congruence transformation. Translations, reflections, and rotations preserve both shape and size.
questions.hint: Congruence transformations preserve size.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Two similar triangles have corresponding sides of lengths 6 units and 9 units. What is the scale factor from the smaller triangle to the larger triangle? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: The scale factor is the ratio of corresponding side lengths, 9 divided by 6, or 1.5. A common error is using 6 divided by 9.
questions.hint: Divide the larger side length by the smaller side length.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: compute area with a circular hole
questions.stem: A square has side length 10 units and contains a circular hole of radius 2 units. Which expression gives the remaining area? Use 3.14 for pi.

options.misconception: adds the hole area instead of subtracting

questions.explanation: Subtract the circle area, pi r squared, from the square area. With radius 2, that is 3.14 times 2 times 2.
questions.hint: Square area minus circle area.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.stem: Two complementary angles sum to 90 degrees. One angle measures 27 degrees. What is the measure of the other angle, in degrees? Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Complementary angles sum to 90 degrees, so the missing angle is 90 minus 27, or 63 degrees. A common error is using 180 degrees instead of 90.
questions.hint: Complementary angles sum to 90 degrees.

questions.subject: GEOMETRY
questions.learningObjective: compute arc length from radius and central angle
questions.stem: A circle has radius 10 units. A central angle of 36 degrees intercepts an arc. What is the length of the arc, in units? Use 3.14 for pi. Report the number only.
questions.explanation: Arc length is circumference times angle over 360, so 2 times 3.14 times 10 times 36/360 equals 6.28 units. A common error is using the full circumference.
questions.hint: Arc length = 2 pi r times (angle/360).
